notes: Champion rule: Per family: lowest selection-backtest WAPE (ratio of sums, 10 origins x 12 stores x 14 days); tie (within 0.05 pp) -> lower |bias|. LightGBM competes with promo variant A (known promo plan).
Actuals are observed sales (units; some families such as produce are fractional), not unconstrained demand: stock-outs are not visible in the data.
The holdout (6 weekly origins, targets 2017-06-28 to 2017-08-15) was scored once, after champions, interval quantiles and Trust Index weights were frozen. Nothing was tuned on it.
Every model is scored on the identical population: open target days with an observed actual.
WAPE and bias are ratios of sums over the slice. Week buckets sum the 7 daily forecasts and actuals per series and origin (days 1–7 and 8–14) before computing the metrics.

Variant A uses the known promotion plan (count of promoted items on the target date); variant B has no future promotion information. Baselines use no promotion information and appear once (variant A).

MAE and RMSE are on the index scale ('index points'): each row's error (actual − forecast) is divided by its series' mean daily sales in the training period (2015-06-01 to 2017-02-06) and multiplied by 100 before averaging, so 1 index point = 1 % of an average training-period day of that series. WAPE and bias are ratios of sums in units, unchanged. Unit volumes are not published (Kaggle rules).
